strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem: bias in LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation that could systematically distort reported model improvements
Sound mathematical framework with rigorous proofs: correct bias analysis, proper derivation of adjusted estimator and confidence intervals using delta method and adjusted Wald approach
Complete statistical treatment: uniquely accounts for uncertainty from both test and calibration datasets, unlike prior work focused only on point estimation
Novel practical contribution: adaptive allocation algorithm (Proposition 2, Algorithm 1) efficiently allocates calibration resources with clear theoretical optimality guarantees
Excellent presentation: clear exposition, intuitive figures (especially Fig. 1-2), logical flow from motivation to methods to validation
Comprehensive empirical validation: extensive Monte Carlo simulations across 16 parameter configurations with 10,000 replications each, with results in main paper and appendix
Practical accessibility: working Python code implementation provided, making adoption straightforward for practitioners
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: core bias correction simply applies classical Rogan-Gladen (1978) estimator; while timely, the statistical techniques are not new
No real-world validation: relies entirely on synthetic Monte Carlo simulations; missing empirical evaluation on actual LLM judgments against human ground truth (e.g., on benchmarks like MTBench)
Restricted scope: limited to binary classification (correct/incorrect); no treatment of multi-class, soft labels, or regression settings common in practice
Theoretical assumptions not fully explored: Proposition 1 assumes symmetric case (m₀=m₁, q₀=q₁); behavior near boundary q₀+q₁=1 and with asymmetric allocations understudied

Limited practical guidance: paper doesn't specify when bias correction matters in practice (e.g., bias magnitude thresholds), how to choose calibration sizes without prior knowledge of q₀, q₁, or how to handle real-world distribution shifts
Missing real-world application example: would benefit from concrete case study before methods section showing the problem on actual data
Incomplete technical details: code repository link appears placeholder ('available at'), no discussion of numerical stability near denominator boundaries or edge case handling
